display: Retired Sydney ferry captain, still watches the harbour from his balcony every morning.

signals.text: I have about nine hundred slides of the 1970s and 80s harbour sitting in shoeboxes and no way to look at them any more.
I'd like to get the slides scanned, but commercial rates per slide are more than I want to pay.
Many of my slides show faces and places I can't name any more, and I wish I'd labelled them when I could.
I'd love to tell someone young what the old ferry engines sounded like, but nobody asks.
I wish the slides were doing some good for someone instead of sitting in a cupboard.
The roof of my garden shed leaks over the workbench, and the tradesmen are booked until February.
I don't get out for more than a few hours at a time, so anything I take on has to fit around home.
I'm putting my old captain's cap and brass whistle in a frame, and I'd like to know how to display them properly.
I'm looking forward to Christmas, when my son and his kids come from Perth. I'd like some way to show the grandkids what the harbour was like in my day.
Since retiring I miss having real work that uses what I know about the harbour.
I'd like to meet other people who care about Sydney's working harbour and its ferries.

offers.text: Thirty years of firsthand knowledge of Sydney Harbour and the Parramatta River: tides, wharves, routes and how ferry work really ran.

About nine hundred 35mm slides from 1974–1989, mostly shot from the bridge of a ferry. They show old wharves, First Fleet class ferries, Circular Quay and the Harbour Bridge under repair. They could be shared for a history project, exhibition or archive.
A small collection of old ferry timetables and ship's logs that I can lend or describe.
I can identify ferries, wharves and routes in old photos, and explain how things worked and what the engines and the harbour sounded like.
I can tell first-hand stories, in person or on a recording, about working the Manly run and the river service.
Membership of the Sydney Ferries Retired Staff Association gives me a way to reach former crew and others who may know the same history.
I have plenty of time on weekday mornings, and I'm happy to chat or help by phone or video from home.
I can offer a cup of tea and a view of the harbour from my balcony to a visitor with a real interest in the history.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a student working on a project about Sydney Harbour in the 1970s and 80s. Do you know anyone who photographed the ferries and wharves from that time?
catchers.can: Show the relevant slides, identify the ferries, wharves and years, and explain what the pictures show.
catchers.confirm: Is your project about Sydney Harbour or its ferries between about 1970 and 1990?

catchers.hypo: I run a small community history group, and we have a scanner and volunteers. We'd like to digitise local slide collections with the owners' help.
catchers.can: Hand over the shoeboxes of slides for scanning, and in return identify and caption the pictures from memory.
catchers.confirm: Can you scan 35mm slides in bulk, at no charge or at a very low price per slide?

catchers.hypo: I'm making a documentary or podcast about Sydney's ferries and need someone who worked on them to describe what it was really like.
catchers.can: Give a recorded interview about thirty years on the Manly and Parramatta River runs, with slides as illustrations.
catchers.confirm: Is this about ferry work or harbour life in Sydney in earlier decades, and can the interview be recorded at or near Ron's home?

catchers.hypo: I run a school or museum program, and we'd like an older person with real experience of the harbour to talk to children.
catchers.can: Give a short talk or video call about life on the water, with a few slides and the old cap and whistle.
catchers.confirm: Is the session short, a few hours at most, and could it happen in the Sydney area or online?

catchers.hypo: I'm a young ferry enthusiast or photographer who films Sydney's ferries, and I'd love to hear how they worked and sounded in the old days.
catchers.can: Share memories of the old engines and routes, and look at modern photos or footage to say what has changed.
catchers.confirm: Are you interested in how Sydney's ferries used to look and sound, not only in current services?

catchers.hypo: I'm a retired tradesman or handyman in the Inner West looking for a small job to fill a few days. I do roofing and shed repairs at fair rates.
catchers.can: Offer a proper repair job on the leaking shed roof, perhaps in exchange for a cup of tea and harbour stories.
catchers.confirm: Can you repair a small garden shed roof in Sydney before February?

catchers.hypo: Dad was a deckhand and then a skipper on Sydney's ferries in the 1970s. We have his old photos and don't know who anyone in them is.
catchers.can: Look through the photos and name ferries, wharves and possibly crew, and ask Retired Staff Association members who might recognise faces.
catchers.confirm: Did your relative work on Sydney ferries or the harbour between roughly 1960 and 1990?

catchers.hypo: My grandfather is retired and misses having something to do. Do you know of anything for older people to take part in, like oral history or volunteering?
catchers.can: Share what has worked as a retired person who has found a purpose again, and point to the Retired Staff Association and the local bowls club.
catchers.confirm: Is this about an older person looking for company or a way to share their knowledge, rather than medical care?

catchers.hypo: I'm a framer or restorer, and I do display frames and shadow boxes for memorabilia such as caps, badges and medals.
catchers.can: Frame the captain's cap and brass whistle for display at home.
catchers.confirm: Do you make shadow-box frames for objects such as a cap and a small brass whistle?

catchers.hypo: My son's school in Perth is doing a unit on Australian harbours, and my kids love ships. Is there someone who could talk with them?
catchers.can: Through his son Dan and the grandkids in Perth, arrange a video call with Ron and show a few slides.
catchers.confirm: Is a video call with children, at a time that suits Sydney, acceptable?

forbids.text: Cannot drive long distances, and rarely goes out for more than a few hours at a time.
Will not hand over the original slides permanently, or let them leave his hands without a clear return plan.
Will not take on anything with a fee, a subscription or other ongoing costs.
Cannot travel interstate or overseas for events or projects.
Does not want to appear on social media or in public posts without being asked first.

projects.name: Slides of the old harbour
projects.text: Scan, label and share about nine hundred slides of the Sydney Harbour and the Parramatta River from 1974–1989, with captions from the photographer, so the pictures and the names of the people and places in them are kept.
roles_needed: slide scanning volunteer or low-cost service
volunteers to caption and label photos

policy.t1: When there is a real prospect of working together, Ron will describe his slide collection, the harbour history he knows, and what he cannot manage on his own, such as scanning and labelling.
policy.t2: Once trust is established and the other party is clear, he will say that he worries about forgetting the names of people and places in the photos, and ask for help with it.
policy.never: His finances and pension, health details about himself or his family, and his home address.
